No blocking performance finding. Reviewed the clean, detached tree at this exact head against the performance packet; no local build, deployment, daemon restart, credential read or pane input.

## Finding

**LOW - measurement scope, not a code defect.** The author's candidate receipts prove the isolated five-seat rig's launch and stalled-upstream behavior; the reviewer's live-host observations are a pre-feature baseline, not a matched production before/after comparison. No production CPU/RSS improvement is established. **Follow-up:** on the authorized rollout, repeat the timed per-operation counters, 20-second machine launch sensor, daemon CPU and RSS on a comparable fleet; preserve daemon identity and separate observer overhead. This is not a request to deploy from a review seat.

## Cost inventory

| Path | Rate and bound | Scaling |
|---|---|---|
| Background readiness | No new timer. The existing lazy check moves off the status await. Healthy TTL 600 s; failed-check TTL 60 s; refresh/402 invalidations and explicit reloads can request earlier checks. Each check makes at most two sequential upstream GETs, each with a 15 s timeout. | One admitted readiness task across all status readers, not one per seat. `try_lock_owned` happens before `tokio::spawn`; losing readers neither spawn a checker nor queue on its lock. Startup/reload share that lock. |
| Daemon watch | Existing one loopback GET per 30 s plus one bulk registry read; zero process launches. | Request count is fleet-independent. Existing descriptor decoding/splitting and cached seat-list storage still scale with live Copilot seats; this PR does not add another per-seat pass. |
| Spawn gate | One GET normally; at most one additional GET after a send/header timeout. Each read is bounded at 1 s. No retry loop, timer or launch. | Per eligible Copilot spawn, not per existing seat. A stalled body is classified unreadable, not retried. |
| Quota response attribution | One account-string capture per forwarding attempt and a short account/generation check. Existing forwarding retries remain bounded to one. | Per response; no prompt-sized copy, extra parse, network request or process launch. |
| Notices and health | Existing state-transition fan-out only. Count-only notice text replaces joining all proxied seat ids; slow counters are constant-size. | Notice text no longer grows with seat ids; recipient fan-out still scales with live primes. Health retains the existing seat list/model map and their serialization costs. |

Anchors: `crates/cache-proxy/src/proxy.rs:438-575,639-693,758-861`; `crates/cache-proxy/src/readiness.rs:21-24,198-230`; `crates/daemon/src/cache_proxy.rs:47,291-308,322-369,442-514,528-647`.

**New process launch sites: zero.** `tokio::spawn` here creates a task, not an OS process. Existing `gh` token-fetch/refresh launches are unchanged. `crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs` already scans the cache-proxy crate as well as daemon crates; its counted-site, absolute-path and retired-launch witnesses passed in exact-head CI.
